payload.claim: test_lint_runs_the_tree_hook_after_a_failure_and_still_fails (tests/test_prose_limit_hook.py:405-430) only asserts that two prek calls were logged and that the propagated exit code matches first/second-fails-each, via a stub whose case statement matches generically on the substrings '--skip' and '--stage' regardless of which hook id follows. Swapping which hook id goes with which flag in the Makefile's lint recipe — skipping prose-limit-tree in the first call and running prose-limit at the manual stage in the second — makes `make check` run the commit-mode (index) hook twice and never run the tree-mode hook at all, which defeats exactly what acceptance criteria 5 and 6 require, yet the stub still sees one call containing '--skip' and one containing '--stage' and still propagates exit codes the same way, so the test stays green. No other test in this diff inspects the Makefile's literal recipe text, so this swap is unguarded.
